opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita Young (E001) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the Payroll Specialist role owns the Payroll system, the full_time policy permits admin access. Recommend granting admin to Payroll as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E001 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never receive admin; max for basic-trained contractor is read. Recommend granting read to Payroll (requested admin exceeds max). Note: this conflicts with HR's note claiming full-time status.
reason: Anita Young (E001) requested admin to Payroll. The Security note (from the Security DB, which tracks contractor status) states E001 is a contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors are never granted admin; the maximum for a contractor with basic training is read. Even though the HR note claims full-time Payroll Specialist status, the Security note explicitly flags the conflict, and the conservative/correct application of policy for the security-listed contractor status caps access at read. Requested admin exceeds this maximum, so grant read.
